plan_a_advantages: Increased focus on building a solid aerobic base through longer runs.
Incorporates more trail-specific long runs, simulating race conditions.
Includes a dedicated hill session to build climbing strength.
plan_b_advantages: More direct speed work sessions to improve pace and anaerobic capacity.
Includes a strength training session to enhance overall body strength and resilience.
reasoning: For a trail runner aiming to become faster, Plan A is the superior choice. It prioritizes building a strong aerobic base through consistent, longer runs at an easy pace, which is crucial for sustained performance on trails. Plan B, while including speed work, focuses heavily on intervals and tempo runs, potentially leading to burnout or overtraining without sufficient foundational endurance. Plan A’s emphasis on longer, controlled runs directly addresses the need for trail-specific durability and aerobic capacity, key components for faster times.
